data.analysis: N stays 3, with the same roles. T1 and T2 risk converging: both may become ordinary tiled SIMT kernels distinguished only by tile parameters. Make T1 include a coalesced one-output-per-thread control to isolate the baseline’s lane-mapping issue, then explore shared-memory CTA tiling. Make T2 explicitly test multiple register accumulators per thread and compare against a one-output-per-thread control. T3 is a useful distinct pipeline investigation, but its sync/async comparison should hold tile and lane mapping constant so it isolates staging rather than confounding it with a different kernel. The source indicates adjacent lanes vary the row index, making A and C accesses strided; B is repeated across those lanes. The only performance evidence remains the valid baseline at 0.2734838867186667 s; no candidate results are available. The CUDA 12.6.3 guide documents async-copy support and its compute-capability qualification, but the target’s runtime capability was not queried. Reference: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html.

revisions.objective: First benchmark a minimal coalesced, row-major one-output-per-thread kernel with lanes varying over columns, to isolate the cost of the supplied baseline’s lane mapping. Then explore synchronous shared-memory CTA tiles using that coalesced orientation and one output per thread, varying tile dimensions and K depth. Support tails and all valid dimensions and values, compute every output with the requested alpha/beta semantics, and report correctness and repeated timing. Use full-FP32 CUDA-core arithmetic only; preserve the entry point and buffer/stream constraints, with no extra allocations or external math libraries.
revisions.subject: Coalescing control plus synchronous SIMT CTA tiling

revisions.objective: Focus on register-blocked SIMT where each thread maintains multiple independent FP32 output accumulators, testing distinct row/column microtile mappings to reuse operands and improve arithmetic intensity. Compare against a one-output-per-thread control so the result is not merely a CTA tile-size comparison with T1; measure register/occupancy tradeoffs and correctness as well as repeated timing. Support tails and all valid dimensions and values, apply alpha/beta once per output, and preserve the entry point, buffers, stream, and full-FP32 requirement. Do not use tensor-core/reduced-precision math, extra allocations, or external math libraries.
revisions.subject: Multi-accumulator register-blocked SIMT microtiles

revisions.objective: Explore whether asynchronous global-to-shared K-stage copies improve a tiled SIMT kernel. Establish a paired synchronous-staging control with the same CTA tile, lane mapping, and compute mapping as the asynchronous version, then compare timings and correctness to isolate the pipeline effect. Handle alignment, completion, synchronization, tails, and any needed fallback for all valid inputs; preserve full-FP32 arithmetic, alpha/beta semantics, entry point, stream, and buffer limits. Use only CUDA 12.6.3-supported mechanisms, no external math libraries, reduced precision, or extra allocations; treat gains as hypotheses to measure.
revisions.subject: Matched synchronous/asynchronous K-stage pipeline comparison

The 4096-square case is the performance focus; every valid call must still compute current inputs correctly, including tails and varied values, within absolute error 0.01. Preserve the host entry point, default stream, and supplied storage; do not assume scratch is initialized, allocate extra memory, call external math libraries, or use TF32/FP16/BF16.
